page: Vultr vx1-g-4c-16g-240s is a general-purpose virtual server belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz. The system includes 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage is provided via a local 240 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU hardware is present.

The x86_64 CPU architecture supports advanced instruction sets including AVX, AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, AVX_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16, which assist with vector calculations and machine learning inference. Cryptographic operations are accelerated via AES, VAES, and SHA_NI instruction sets. The processor features a 32 MB L3 cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache, with hardware virtualization enabled via AMD SVM.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU metrics, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression all placing in the top 10% tier. However, multi-core scaling presents a tradeoff; the multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and Geekbench multi-core scores fall into the bottom 25% tier, reflecting the physical 2-core, 4-thread topology. Memory bandwidth and database operations, including Redis SET operations at 8.1 million operations per second, consistently perform in the average middle 50% tier.

This server configuration offers a balanced resource density suitable for general-purpose workloads, web serving, and lightweight database operations. While it handles small-model LLM inference at average speeds, prompt processing for medium-sized 7B models is poor, placing in the bottom 10% tier. The instance is best suited for single-threaded tasks, static web serving, software compilation, and applications requiring dedicated CPU allocation with local NVMe storage, rather than highly parallelized multi-threaded compute.

Operating at 2.0 GHz across 2 physical cores with hyper-threading, the CPU supports AVX-512 and cryptographic instruction sets.
